title: Measures to Mitigate Effects of Extreme Weather Conditions
what_it_is: Measures to Mitigate Effects of Extreme Weather Conditions

sections.label: Heat impact on vulnerable groups
sections.summary: Questions ask what measures, studies and long-term plans address heat impacts on vulnerable groups and heat inequality.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in view of the changing climate and increasing frequency of extreme weather events, in particular extreme heat, what targeted measures are being taken to mitigate the impact of these events on heat vulnerable groups, such as the elderly or lower income groups, who are more at risk of adverse effects, due to physiological or social obstacles to cooling solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether studies are being conducted or will be conducted to better understand the distribution of heat and energy inequality in our communities; and (b) what are the long-term plans to build heat resilient communities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether Singapore's island-wide temperature and urban heat island projections require revision in light of the ongoing climate crisis and recent heat waves reported around the world; and (b) what projections exist for how future temperature trends will affect (i) indoor temperatures (ii) building ventilation requirements and (iii) usage of air-conditioning.

sections.label: CCRS temperature projections
sections.summary: The Centre for Climate Research Singapore projects average temperatures rising 1.4 to 4.6 degrees Celsius by end of century, with 40 degree days possibly by 2045.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Centre for Climate Research Singapore, CCRS for short, has projected that climate change would lead to average temperatures rising by 1.4 to 4.6 degrees Celsius by the end of the century.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Days with peak temperatures of 40 degrees Celsius may appear as early as 2045.

sections.label: Climate drivers and V3 study
sections.summary: Singapore is affected by climate drivers like El Nino, and projections are being reviewed and updated through the Third National Climate Change Study next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: For example, while we do not experience the extreme temperatures arising from high pressure systems that form across large continental masses in the mid-latitude region, we are affected by climate drivers such as El Niño, that are likely to be exacerbated by climate change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: These projections are being reviewed and will be updated through the Third National Climate Change Study, or "V3", that will be released next year.

sections.label: Energy efficiency and community resilience
sections.summary: Using less electricity reduces heat and carbon emissions, so energy efficiency is encouraged, including the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: When we use less electricity, we not only reduce the heat emitted from our own electrical appliances, we also reduce the energy that needs to be generated by our power stations, thereby reducing both heat generation and carbon emissions at the system level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Hence, we have been enhancing community resilience to climate change by encouraging businesses and individuals to adopt greater energy efficiency, such as the introduction of the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme to help consumers choose more energy-efficient appliances.
